space_applied.note: Both: SPACE is the review's analytical lens (Section 3.6, with TCE). In the text the lens is declared but findings are not organized dimension by dimension; author should confirm.

ai_discussed.note: AI coding assistants and agentic tools are the topic.

remote_covid.note: Neither mentions remote work or COVID-19.

data_window.claude: Review coverage January 2022–April 2026 (search February–April 2026); pilot four months, undated
data_window.note: NotebookLM gives 2022–2026 without months; pilot period not dated by either.

cat_productivity.note: Task completion speed, tasks completed and throughput synthesized as the individual side of the PRP.

cat_quality.note: Change failure rate, defect density, bug counts, delivery stability, code quality dimensions; pilot hotfixes and rollbacks.

cat_collaboration.note: PR review time (+91%) and the code review bottleneck as an amplifying mechanism.

cat_satisfaction.note: Well-being only noted as understudied; pilot measures confidence, not satisfaction.

cat_activity.note: Merged PRs, PR size, LOC, suggestion acceptance, code churn.

cat_delivery.note: DORA delivery metrics, cycle time, pilot median lead time per feature.

cat_agile.note: Thin basis: AAMT treats Agile (sprint velocity, iteration compression); pilot reports hotfixes per sprint.

cat_survey.note: Pilot Likert questionnaires (developer confidence 3.1 to 3.9) and interviews; cited developer surveys.

evidence.quote: Through a multivocal systematic literature review encompassing 67 sources (29 peer-reviewed studies, 18 pre-prints, 12 structured industry reports, and 8 grey literature sources), published between January 2022 and April 2026
Since 2022, the rapid adoption of AI-powered coding assistants has produced a striking empirical contradiction

controlled studies report individual-level productivity gains of 20-56% on well-scoped tasks, while the most rigorous randomized controlled trial to date documents a 19% slowdown for experienced developers on mature codebases
The SPACE framework (Forsgren et al. 2021) organizes productivity and quality findings along the five dimensions of Satisfaction, Performance, Activity, Communication, and Efficiency.

output metrics (task completion speed, lines of code, suggestion acceptance rates) that coexist with statistically significant degradation in system-level dependability metrics (delivery stability, change failure rate, code churn, defect density in production).

When AI tools accelerate individual code generation without proportional acceleration of the review pipeline, the result is a growing queue of unreviewed pull requests that absorbs the productivity gains at the organizational level
Organizational-level DORA metrics (deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate) showed no measurable improvement despite the individual-level gains.

At Tier 2, the sprint velocity increase observed in multiple studies (Smit et al. 2024: +10.6% PRs) creates pressure to compress iteration cycles, potentially accelerating the cadence without ensuring that verification keeps pace.
triangulated with semi-structured interviews and brief Likert-scale questionnaires administered at the end of each phase.
